extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (health care providers, health insurers), legal counsel, and other stakeholders subject to or commenting on Section 1557 nondiscrimination rules
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and regulatory guidance interpreting Section 1557 nondiscrimination obligations for health programs and activities, including provider conduct, coverage design, marketing, and enforcement frameworks. Covers how OCR will evaluate denials of care, insurance coverage practices, and related exemptions (e.g., religious/conscience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to clinician judgment about medical appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR has a general practice of deferring to a clinician's judgment about whether a particular service is medically appropriate for an individual, or whether the clinician has the appropriate expertise to provide care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in section 1557 compels clinicians to provide a service they do not believe is medically appropriate for a patient or that they are not qualified to provide. However, OCR will examine whether an asserted clinical judgment is pretextual or reflects unlawful animus or bias when investigating discrimination claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered entity determinations must not be based on unlawful animus or bias
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity's determination must not be based on unlawful animus or bias, or constitute a pretext for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will consider the covered entity's rationale for denying care, any supporting information offered, and any evidence of unlawful animus, bias, or other discriminatory factors. The revised §92.206(c) explicitly states this standard and notes it does not preclude protections described in §§92.3 and 92.302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason framework for denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities facing allegations of discrimination may articulate a legitimate, nondiscriminatory basis for their challenged action or practice; such a basis may not be a pretext for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes that a provider may have a legitimate nondiscriminatory reason not to provide a health service (e.g., religious objection applied uniformly), but will assess whether the reason is pretextual or discriminatorily applied. In investigations, OCR will evaluate whether the asserted clinical appropriateness reflects unlawful animus or bias or is a pretext (example: pain medication denied due to stereotyping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden-of-proof and methods of proof (Arlington Heights and McDonnell Douglas frameworks)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will use different methods of proof drawn from civil rights case law, including the Arlington Heights multi-factor test and the McDonnell Douglas burden-shifting framework, to analyze discrimination claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason' is taken from but should not be construed to limit proof to McDonnell Douglas. Arlington Heights allows use of direct, circumstantial, statistical, and anecdotal evidence together; McDonnell Douglas is commonly applied to inferential proof in individual disparate treatment cases where comparator evidence may be considered but is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition (non-definition) of gender-affirming care in rule text
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to provide a regulatory definition for 'gender-affirming care' in the rule text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used in §§92.206 and 92.207, OCR generally refers to care designed to treat gender dysphoria that may include, but is not necessarily limited to, counseling, hormone therapy, surgery, and other related services. The rule does not impose a categorical requirement that covered entities must provide gender-affirming care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom and conscience objections may be legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may have religious or conscience objections to providing certain types of care; such objections can serve as a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason where they are neither pretextual nor discriminatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a provider typically declines a particular service for any individual based on a religious belief, regardless of sex assigned at birth or gender identity, the provider likely meets §92.206(c)'s standard for a 'legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason.' Where religious belief causes differential treatment, providers may rely on protections afforded by religious freedom and conscience laws or seek assurance through §92.302(b)'s exemption process. §92.206(c) was amended to reference §92.302 explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR will not set a standard of care; rule does not interfere with individualized clinical judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not (and cannot) require a specific standard of care or course of treatment for any individual, and section 1557 does not interfere with individualized clinical judgment about appropriate care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The focus of investigations will be whether an asserted clinical judgment reflects unlawful animus or bias or is pretextual, not a general review of clinical decisionmaking. OCR defers to clinicians' judgments about medical appropriateness and expertise subject to the discrimination analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harassment/hostile environment standard is fact-specific; severity/pervasiveness threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether discrimination is unlawful or considered harassment is necessarily fact-specific; it is unlikely that an isolated incident with no other indications of animus or ill treatment would meet the standards for discriminatory harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct, including verbal harassment, that is so severe or pervasive that it creates a hostile environment on the basis of sex is a form of sex discrimination under the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption and consideration of state/local law compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557's nondiscrimination requirements generally preempt conflicting State or local laws that restrict access to care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In enforcement, OCR will consider the specific factual record of each complaint, including whether a covered entity acted in good faith believing it was obligated by State or local law, whether it demonstrated willingness to refer or provide accurate information about care, or engaged in good faith efforts to ensure delivery of medically necessary care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination in health insurance coverage and related practices (§92.207 general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities that provide or administer health insurance coverage and other health-related coverage and receive Federal financial assistance are prohibited from discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in the provision or administration of such coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §92.207(a) sets the general nondiscrimination requirement; §92.207(d) clarifies that enumerated examples do not limit the general prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on denials, cancellations, limits, or additional cost sharing on protected bases (§92.207(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are prohibited from denying, cancelling, limiting, or refusing to issue or renew health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage, denying or limiting coverage of a claim, or imposing additional cost sharing or other limitations or restrictions on coverage on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost sharing is standard industry practice, but it cannot be imposed in a discriminatory manner. Comments regarding EHB requirements are outside the scope of this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory marketing practices and benefit designs (§92.207(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR proposed prohibiting marketing practices or benefit designs that discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination whether a marketing practice is prohibited requires case-by-case analysis. Inaccuracies or omissions intended to or resulting in discouraging individuals from enrolling or steering individuals away on a prohibited basis would raise concerns of prohibited discrimination (example: avoiding advertising in areas populated by a majority of people of color). OCR declined to enumerate specific regulatory examples but noted an example in the Proposed Rule. OCR also noted coordination with other agencies and the need for accessible materials for LEP individuals and persons with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on categorical coverage exclusions for gender-affirming care (§92.207(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are prohibited from having or implementing a categorical coverage exclusion or limitation for all health services related to gender transition or other gender-affirming care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to address systemic denials of coverage for services related to gender transition; OCR invited comment on scope and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory limits on coverage for specific gender-transition services (§92.207(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may not impose discriminatory limits on coverage for specific health services related to gender transition or other gender-affirming care, which generally would be the case if such limits are not applied when those same health services are not related to gender transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR invited comment on whether §92.207(b)(5) sufficiently addresses challenges transgender and gender nonconforming individuals face when coverage is affected by discordance between sex assigned at birth and sex as recorded by the issuer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration requirement for persons with disabilities in benefit design (§92.207(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are prohibited from having or implementing a benefit design that does not provide or administer health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR sought comment on benefit design features that result in unjustified segregation or institutionalization, application to post-acute and mental health services, Medicaid compliance under title XIX, and the time needed to reach compliance via reimbursement, service scope, and authorization changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage decisions may rely on legitimate, nondiscriminatory coverage/medical necessity requirements (§92.207(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in §92.207 requires the coverage of any health service where the covered entity has a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for determining that such health service fails to meet applicable coverage requirements, such as medical necessity requirements, in an individual case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes that coverage may permissibly be denied for non-discriminatory reasons tied to plan terms or medical necessity, but such reasons must not be pretextual or discriminatorily applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR investigative focus — discerning pretext vs. legitimate clinical judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The focus of any OCR investigation will not be to generally review a covered entity's clinical judgment but rather to determine whether the assertion of that judgment reflects unlawful animus or bias, or is a pretext for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of pretextual invocations of clinical appropriateness include evidence showing that a covered entity asserted a service was not clinically appropriate because of biased beliefs (example: denying pain medication due to belief women exaggerate pain). OCR will consider the covered entity's rationale, supporting information, and evidence of discriminatory factors in the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of marketing and plan materials for LEP individuals and persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP) or disabilities may face challenges accessing a covered entity's marketing materials; materials must be accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR noted this concern in the context of marketing practices and the potential for discriminatory impacts when materials are inaccessible, implying covered entities should ensure accessible communications to avoid discrimination.
